The update of the\n//     trailing rows for one panel is then a GEMM-like operation (register\n//     blocked, vectorized over the rows), while each individual matrix element\n//     is still the result of one dot product accumulated in ascending k order\n//     by a single rank.  The floating point operations per element and their\n//     order are therefore identical to the sequential reference algorithm.\n//   * Per panel there is exactly one broadcast (the pb x j1 panel block), i.e.\n//     n/NB messages instead of one per column.\n//   * Look-ahead: after receiving panel p, the owner of panel p+1 first updates\n//     its own rows and factors panel p+1, starts the non-blocking broadcast and\n//     only then updates its remaining rows, overlapping communication with\n//     computation.\n\nnamespace {\n\n// Panel width (rows per distribution block / columns per update step).\nconstexpr size_t NB = 32;\n// Register blocking of the trailing update: RB rows x CB columns.\nconstexpr size_t RB = 8;\nconstexpr size_t CB = 4;\n\nint g_rank = 0;\nint g_nranks = 1;\n\ninline size_t panelsOf(const size_t n) { return (n + NB - 1) / NB; positive definite matrix.\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& Aloc, const size_t n, const size_t ldl, const size_t nloc) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B (identical on every rank, so no communication)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n\n    // Compute the locally The update of the\n//     trailing rows for one panel is then a GEMM-like operation (register\n//     blocked, vectorized over the rows), while each individual matrix element\n//     is still the result of one dot product accumulated in ascending k order\n//     by a single rank.   // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate l0 < hi; l0 += RB) {\n        const size_t nr = std::min(RB, hi - l0);\n        const double* __restrict A = Aloc + l0;\n\n        // Phase 1: contributions of the already finished columns k < j0.\n        if (j0 > 0) {\n            // Pack the RB x j0 slice of the local matrix contiguously; c < pb; ++c) {\n                for (size_t r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {\n                    acc[c * RB + r] = 0.0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Phase 2: the columns inside the panel, in ascending order.  Column\n        // j0 + jj continues the very same accumulator with k = j0 .. j0+jj-1.\n        // The freshly computed columns are kept in a small local buffer so that\n        // this phase works entirely out of L1.\n        double res[NB * RB];\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < pb; ++jj) {\n            const double* __restrict Rj = R + jj * lenR;\n            double* __restrict a = acc + jj * RB;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < jj; ++k) {\n                const double* __restrict col = res + k * RB;\n                const double rv = Rj[j0 + k];\n                for (size_t r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {\n                    a[r] += col[r] * rv;\n                }\n            }\n            const double d = Rj[j0 + jj];\n            const double* __restrict colj = Aloc + (j0 + jj) * ldl + l0;\n            double* __restrict out = res + jj * RB;\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {\n                out[r] = (colj[r] - a[r]) / d;\n            }\n        }\n        for (size_t jj = 0; jj < pb; ++jj) {\n            const double* __restrict src = res + jj * RB;\n            double* __restrict colj = Aloc + (j0 + jj) * ldl + l0;\n            for (size_t r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {\n                colj[r] = src[r];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Factor the diagonal block of the panel starting at global row j0 (pb rows,\n// local rows [lq, lq + pb)) and pack the finished panel rows (columns\n// 0 .. j0+pb-1) into R.  Returns false if the matrix is not positive definite.\n// The status is encoded as 1.0 on success and -(failing column + 1) otherwise.\ndouble factorPanel(double* __restrict Aloc, const size_t ldl, const size_t lq, const size_t j0, const size_t pb,\n    double* __restrict R, const size_t lenR) {\n    // Gather the already computed part of the panel rows. The owner of a panel factors its diagonal block locally and broadcasts the finished `pb × j1` block (one message per panel, `n/NB` total instead of one per column).\n2. Every rank then updates its trailing rows: a register-blocked GEMM (8 rows × 4 cols, compiler vector extensions, BLIS-style packing of the row slice) for the columns `k < j0`, then the in-panel columns out of an L1 buffer.\n3. **Look-ahead**: after receiving panel `p`, the owner of panel `p+1` updates and factors its own rows first and posts an `MPI_Ibcast`, so that communication overlaps the bulk trailing update.\n\nMatrix generation (`A = B·Bᵀ`) is also distributed by rows and register-tiled; validation is done row-distributed with an `MPI_Allreduce(MAX)`; `-r` gathers the full factor on rank 0.\n\n**Semantics** — each matrix element is still one dot product accumulated over ascending `k` by a single rank, so no reduction is reordered. Verified: with `-ffp-contract=off` on both, the output is **bitwise identical to the original sequential code** for n ∈ {1,5,33,100,400,513,1000} × 1/3/8/17/40 ranks. With the project's default flags the result differs from the sequential build by ≤ 4e-13 relative — smaller than the original's own sensitivity to that flag (2.5e-13 vs. its own contraction-off build), and the output is identical for every rank count. Validation passes and hashes are rank-count-independent; the non-positive-definite path prints the same message and exit code on all ranks.\n\n## Measured (EPYC 7763, 128 cores, vs. the original sequential build)\n\n| n | seq | 1 rank | 8 | 32 | 64 | 128 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 4096 | 17865 ms | 3083 ms | 486 ms | **321 ms (56×)** | 362 ms | 393 ms |\n| 8192 | ~143 s (est.) | 31.7 s | 4085 ms | 1542 ms | **1254 ms (~114×)** | 1410 ms |\n\nSingle-rank is already ~5.8× the original from the blocked/vectorized kernel; `NB` was picked by sweeping 16/24/32/64 across rank counts. n=4096 saturates around 16–32 ranks (the panel-factor chain becomes the critical path); the larger problem keeps scaling to 64+.
